display: I run a non-profit community music school in Scarborough, Toronto.

signals.text: We have a waitlist of 30 kids for piano lessons and nowhere good to put them.
Our two practice rooms only have digital keyboards, and our teachers say the kids can't learn real acoustic touch on them.
A decent acoustic upright costs more than our whole yearly equipment budget, so I've been looking for any way around buying one new.
I'm looking for a used acoustic piano, or someone who could help move and tune one cheaply.
The building's heating is poor and the landlord says it's 'within code', while the kids' fingers are cold in winter.
I've logged a month of room temperatures but don't know if that counts as evidence, and we have no lawyer.
I'm writing three grant applications this fall, mostly late at night, and my writing keeps sounding like a slide deck.
The funder wants 'measurable outcomes' for something like a kid falling in love with music, and I can't find the words.
I spend more time as a grant writer than as a musician and I miss playing.
I'm trying to get a one-page attendance and impact summary together for a sponsor.
My Sunday cover band has a wedding gig in November and our timing in a couple of songs is shaky.
September attendance hit a record, and I want more families to know about the school without turning anyone away over fees.

offers.text: I can teach and talk about running a sliding-scale community music school: pricing, teacher hiring, recitals and keeping classes affordable.
Cello and bass playing, including session or band work, from a decade of freelancing.
A school with 11 part-time teachers and about 140 students a week, which could host a workshop, pop-up concert or pilot programme.
Two small practice rooms and a larger room with a drum kit and amps in a former bank branch (the vault is the drum room), available for rehearsals or small events at off-peak times.
Working relationships with the TDSB music coordinator, two churches that lend halls for recitals, and a local credit union that sponsors our spring concert.
A seniors' singing circle on Thursday mornings, which could host visiting singers, accompanists or intergenerational sessions.
Experience writing grants for Ontario arts and community funders, which I can share with other small non-profits.
A cover band (The Overdrafts) that plays weddings and community events.

catchers.hypo: Hi, we're clearing out my late mother's Yamaha upright in the GTA and want it to go to kids rather than a landfill. Do you know anyone who'd take it?
catchers.can: The school would gladly take a good acoustic piano for the waitlisted kids and will arrange the move and tuning.
catchers.confirm: Is the piano an acoustic upright or grand in playable condition, located in the Greater Toronto Area?

catchers.hypo: I run a small piano moving and tuning business and have some slack days. Do any community groups need a piano relocated at a discount?
catchers.can: I can line up a used piano purchase or donation and use your discounted move and tuning, which is currently the main cost barrier.
catchers.confirm: Could you move and tune a piano in the Toronto area for much less than commercial rates, for a non-profit?

catchers.hypo: I'm a piano teacher with a few free hours a week who'd like to volunteer with kids who can't afford lessons.
catchers.can: I can introduce you to our piano teacher Marcus and the waitlist, and we can discuss a volunteer or low-cost group-lesson pilot.
catchers.confirm: Are you a trained piano teacher able to commit weekly hours in Scarborough, not just occasional help?

catchers.hypo: I'm a tenant lawyer, or paralegal, and I do pro bono work for non-profits stuck in landlord disputes over building conditions.
catchers.can: I can share my temperature logs and correspondence and ask for advice on what counts as evidence for heating problems.
catchers.confirm: Do you have experience with commercial tenancy or building-code disputes in Ontario, not only residential tenancies?

catchers.hypo: I used to write for the Ontario Arts Council and could review a draft application for a small arts group.
catchers.can: I can show you my OAC draft and ask for feedback on turning stories into measurable outcomes.
catchers.confirm: Have you read or assessed OAC or similar Ontario arts grant applications before?

catchers.hypo: I lead a seniors' choir and would love to share songs, volunteers or a joint concert with another group.
catchers.can: The Thursday seniors' circle could join in a joint session, and the school could host or accompany.
catchers.confirm: Does your group sing regularly with older adults and could it visit Scarborough on a weekday morning?

catchers.hypo: My family just arrived in Toronto and my child is always humming and tapping on tables. Are there affordable music lessons nearby?
catchers.can: Our school never turns kids away over fees, and I can place the child with a teacher, or send them to a friendly newcomer-support contact.
catchers.confirm: Is the child between about 5 and 17, living in or near Scarborough, and in need of low-cost lessons?

catchers.hypo: We need a bass player who can read charts for a few shows, and we play mostly funk and soul covers.
catchers.can: I play bass and may be able to sit in, or I can recommend someone from my band's circle.
catchers.confirm: Are these weekend or evening gigs in the Toronto area, with a rehearsal schedule that avoids Tuesday and Thursday evenings?

forbids.text: I won't turn kids away from lessons because of fees.
I can't work evenings on Tuesdays or Thursdays.
I can't commit to anything that needs spending real money quickly, as the school only funds major purchases through planned approvals.
I'm based in Toronto and the school is in Scarborough, so I can't do in-person work far outside the GTA.
I won't use students' or their families' personal stories in fundraising without their consent.

projects.name: Piano programme
projects.text: Get an acoustic piano into the school so the 30 waitlisted kids can learn on a real instrument, through a donation, a used purchase, or a sponsor.

projects.name: Fall grant cycle
projects.text: Three grant applications due on 15 October, 31 October and 14 November, including a hard-to-write impact section.

projects.name: Heating dispute
projects.text: Get a commercial landlord to fix inadequate heating in a community school, using month-long temperature logs.
roles_needed: pro bono tenancy or building-code adviser

policy.t1: When there are signs of a fit, I'll share details of the school's programmes, the piano waitlist and costs, the grant work, the heating dispute and my cover band.
policy.t2: Once I trust the other party and know who they are, I'll talk about my worries over the school's long-term survival and how heavy the admin load is.
policy.never: My personal finances and the school board's internal politics and decisions.
